_comment: Merge these into your Firebase Realtime Database rules. Locks down the reel comment system, which previously had ZERO enforcement of its own — every edit/delete/pin/report restriction lived only in ReelCommentFragment.java's UI code, so any authenticated client (or a raw REST call) could edit/delete anyone's comment, fake-pin things, or tamper with commentsCount.
_instructions: 1. Open Firebase Console -> Realtime Database -> Rules tab
2. Merge the 'rules' object below into your existing rules JSON

3. CRITICAL: this only works if your root rule is NOT a blanket "auth != null" write for everything. In Firebase RTDB, if ANY ancestor node grants .write:true, that permission cascades down and OVERRIDES any narrower rule written below it. If your deployed rules (see firebase_rules_deployed_updated_v2.json) currently have a top-level ".write": "auth != null", these nested rules are silently bypassed. You must either (a) remove/narrow that blanket top-level write so each path opts in explicitly, or (b) move these paths under a root that doesn't already grant blanket write access.

4. reelCommentReports / reelReplyReports are intentionally NOT readable by normal users (no admin-role concept exists yet in these rules) — read them from a trusted backend/Cloud Function, or add an isAdmin check once you have one.

$commentId._comment_write: Only two whole-node operations are allowed here: CREATE (must not already exist, and the new row's uid must be the author) and DELETE (comment owner OR the reel's owner can remove it). Edits go through the per-field rules below, not this one.
$commentId..write: auth != null && ((!data.exists() && newData.exists() && newData.child('uid').val() === auth.uid) || (data.exists() && !newData.exists() && (data.child('uid').val() === auth.uid || root.child('reels').child($reelId).child('uid').val() === auth.uid)))
$commentId..validate: !newData.exists() || (newData.hasChildren(['commentId','uid','ownerName','text','timestamp']) && newData.child('commentId').val() === $commentId && newData.child('uid').val() === auth.uid && newData.child('text').isString() && newData.child('text').val().length > 0 && newData.child('text').val().length <= 300)

text._comment: Editing an existing comment's text: only the original author, and only once the row already exists (creation is covered by the parent .write above).

isPinned._comment: Only the reel's owner can pin/unpin — matches togglePin()'s isReelOwner check, now enforced server-side too.

$uid._comment: A like is just your own uid -> true under the comment. Anyone can write, but ONLY under their own uid, and only a boolean.

$replyId..write: auth != null && ((!data.exists() && newData.exists() && newData.child('uid').val() === auth.uid) || (data.exists() && !newData.exists() && (data.child('uid').val() === auth.uid || root.child('reels').child($reelId).child('uid').val() === auth.uid)))
$replyId..validate: !newData.exists() || (newData.hasChildren(['replyId','parentCommentId','uid','ownerName','text','timestamp']) && newData.child('replyId').val() === $replyId && newData.child('uid').val() === auth.uid && newData.child('text').isString() && newData.child('text').val().length > 0 && newData.child('text').val().length <= 300)

reelCommentReports._comment: Reports are write-once (create only, no edit/delete) and only ever created under the reporter's own claim. Nobody can read the list back through client rules — pull it from a trusted backend.

commentsCount._comment: Kept permissive on WHO can write (any authed viewer's like/comment/delete action touches this via a transaction) but validated so it can't be set to something absurd like a negative number or a non-integer.
